xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2647: fix(health): replace false-positive system health model and harden Health page contract

plan.title: fix(health): replace false-positive system health model and harden Health page contract
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: The dashboard has multiple incompatible health models that report healthy or intentionally idle states as degraded: historical swap occupancy directly drives warning/critical severity, the first sample bypasses hysteresis, reasons and severity can contradict each other, every 30-minute-idle live session is called 'stuck', error/stale agents inflate spawn capacity counts, the server emits agent status 'wedged' that the frontend cannot render (page crash), leaked-specialist detection consumes an always-empty array, and route failures become HTTP 200 empty 'healthy' results. First-time users on healthy machines see everything red.
narratives.Proposal: Lower the implementation PRD (drafts/pan-2647.md on overdeck-state) into one canonical, platform-aware health model: a runtime-validated SystemHealthSnapshot V2 contract in packages/contracts with four separate domains (host pressure, spawn admission, agent runtime, service availability); Linux/macOS platform collectors using current-pressure signals (PSI, swap-activity deltas, memory_pressure -Q, real CPU deltas) with per-signal unavailability; atomic three-sample hysteresis with a neutral 'measuring' cold start; lifecycle-aware agent health through the canonical agent resolver; all routes/UI/spawn-gate/events projecting from the one accepted snapshot; an explicit no-loss audit; Playwright + throwaway Node 22 boot verification; and documentation of signal semantics.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Redesign the entire Resources page or Command Deck
- Change the memory governor's configured soft/hard/recovery reserves or its shedding policy
- Add destructive automatic cleanup from the health UI
- Windows-native support; unsupported platforms return explicit unavailable signals
- Treat cost, disk capacity, Docker stack health, model-provider health, or tracker availability as host memory pressure
- Remove pan doctor or its diagnostic checks
- Remove legacy summary/route fields in this issue (compatibility cycle retained; removal is a follow-up)
- Restart or hot-patch the live dashboard during implementation

autoDecisions.summary: Kept one vBRIEF for this issue instead of splitting into sibling issues.
autoDecisions.rationale: Every slice depends on the shared V2 contract and the final no-loss matrix gates the whole refactor; sibling issues would leave main in mixed-model states between merges and the PRD is written as one coherent no-loss replacement.

autoDecisions.summary: PRD checkpoint 1 (macOS fixture capture) resolved via sanitized fixtures with fail-closed parsing; no live macOS capture.
autoDecisions.rationale: This environment is Linux-only. The PRD's stated fallback applies: accept both verified memory_pressure -Q output shapes as fixtures, and any unrecognized output parses to explicit 'unavailable' rather than guessed values.

autoDecisions.summary: Existing PAN_HEALTH_* environment overrides are retained, parsed through the single finite-number validator, and surfaced in the snapshot.
autoDecisions.rationale: PRD section 2 says 'Environment overrides, if retained' — retaining them matches the no-loss posture; deprecated swap/overcommit thresholds stay readable but inert per the compatibility decision.

autoDecisions.summary: Removal of the duplicate frontend SystemHealthSnapshot interface happens in the frontend-hook migration task, not the contract task.
autoDecisions.rationale: Each task must leave the tree typechecking; deleting the frontend interface before frontend imports migrate would break the build mid-plan.

autoDecisions.summary: requiresInspection set on exactly two foundations: the shared contract (deep) and the agent-health classifier (fast).
autoDecisions.rationale: The contract is the cross-cutting schema every downstream task encodes assumptions about; the classification order determines route, guardrail, and UI behavior. All other tasks are leaves whose defects surface at typecheck/review.

items.title: Add shared SystemHealthSnapshot V2 contract with compatibility projector

narrative.Action: Create packages/contracts/src/system-health.ts per the PRD 'Shared contract' section: HealthState literal ('measuring'|'healthy'|'warning'|'critical'|'unavailable'), HealthReason struct (stable code, domain, severity, message, optional metric/observed/threshold), SystemHealthSnapshot with version 2, overall state, updatedAt, nextPollMs, host domain (state/platform/reasons/metrics), admission domain (open|soft|blocked|unavailable, availableMemoryBytes, admittedWorkAgentCount, reasons), agents array (exhaustive AgentHealthSnapshot statuses: healthy, idle, waiting, warning, stalled, wedged, dead, unavailable), services array (running, not_configured, degraded, stopped, unavailable), topConsumers, and a LegacySystemHealthSummary compatibility projection. Write a pure legacy-summary projector that maps a V2 snapshot to every existing summary field. Export from packages/contracts/src/index.ts. Unknown enum values must decode to explicit unavailable entries, not throw.

Create collector interface and Linux platform collector with fixture-driven parsers

expected_outputs: linux.test.ts passes: healthy-historical-swap, active-swapping, PSI elevated/full, malformed/missing PSI, zero swap, CPU delta cases

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/system-health/types.ts with the HostHealthCollector interface ({ platform: 'linux'|'darwin'|'unsupported', sample(previous?) }) and HostMetricSample types carrying per-signal availability. Implement linux.ts: MemAvailable + total from /proc/meminfo; CPU utilization as delta of aggregate /proc/stat counters; current memory pressure from /proc/pressure/memory some.avg10/full.avg10 when present; swap activity as delta/time of /proc/vmstat pswpin+pswpout; swap occupancy, load averages, Committed_AS, and CommitLimit as diagnostic-only fields. All file/process reads go behind injectable async adapters; parsers are pure functions over fixture strings. Missing or malformed signals (e.g. no PSI in a container) yield explicit per-signal 'unavailable', never zero. collector.ts selects the platform adapter and returns an 'unsupported' collector elsewhere. Named default pressure-band constants live in this module per the PRD. Build the parent-to-children process index once per refresh for memory attribution (NFR-5).

If memory_pressure or a delta signal is unavailable, mark that signal unavailable and let admission fall back to available-memory only — never substitute zero. All subprocess calls use bounded-timeout async exec behind injectable adapters.

Implement pure host-pressure evaluation with structured reason codes

expected_outputs: evaluate.test.ts passes threshold-boundary and diagnostic-only swap/commit cases

narrative.Action: Implement evaluateHostPressure(sample, resolvedThresholds) in src/lib/system-health/evaluate.ts as a pure function producing a raw assessment: HealthState plus structured HealthReason entries (stable codes, domain, severity, observed/threshold values). Encode the PRD default bands: Linux warning when memory.some.avg10 >= 5 or swap activity >= 64 MiB/min while MemAvailable is below the warning reserve; Linux critical when memory.full.avg10 >= 1 or swap activity >= 256 MiB/min while below the critical reserve; macOS warning/critical at <=10%/<=5% memory_pressure free. Available-memory reserve crossings feed the admission domain; they raise host severity only when corroborated by a current-pressure signal. Historical swap occupancy and Committed_AS/CommitLimit never produce a reason with severity above info. On a platform with no current-pressure signal, host state is 'unavailable' while admission reports honestly.

items.title: Given abundant MemAvailable with 50% swap occupancy and quiet pressure signals, When evaluated, Then the assessment returns healthy with no warning/critical reason and swap occupancy appears only in diagnostics

Given samples exactly at each PRD band boundary (some.avg10=5, full.avg10=1, 64/256 MiB/min swap activity, 10%/5% macOS free), When evaluated, Then each boundary produces its documented severity with a stable reason code carrying observed and threshold values
Given low available memory but no elevated current-pressure signal, When evaluated, Then the admission domain reports the reserve crossing while host severity stays below warning
Given a sample whose current-pressure signals are all unavailable, When evaluated, Then host state is unavailable (not healthy, not critical) and admission still reports from available memory
Implement singleton sampler and atomic three-sample hysteresis state machine

expected_outputs: sampler.test.ts passes cold-measuring, escalation/recovery, atomicity, invalid-sample, single-flight, and poll-interval cases using fake timers

narrative.Action: Implement transitionAcceptedAssessment(previous, raw) as a pure state machine: three consecutive samples in a new band are required for both escalation and recovery; the accepted result publishes state, structured reasons, and metrics atomically from the same accepted evaluation; missing/invalid samples do not count toward a transition and cannot clear the previous accepted state (freshness is annotated instead). Implement the singleton sampler in sampler.ts: on first request return a valid 'measuring' snapshot and start warm-up (three samples one second apart), then the configured poll interval; concurrent readers share one sampler (single-flight). Wire system-health-service.ts to consume the accepted assessment, removing the first-sample hysteresis bypass and the severity-only hysteresis. Emit a versioned transition only when the accepted state changes. ALL timing tests use vi.useFakeTimers() + vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync() — real waits are forbidden by repo rule.

items.title: Given a fresh service, When the first health request arrives, Then it returns a valid snapshot with state 'measuring' and starts exactly one sampler regardless of concurrent callers

Given three consecutive samples in a higher band (advanced via fake timers), When the third is accepted, Then state, reasons, and metrics all change together in one accepted assessment — no intermediate mixed publication

Given an accepted warning state and two recovery samples followed by an invalid sample, When evaluated, Then the accepted state remains warning — invalid samples neither count toward nor clear a transition
Given an accepted state change, When the transition publishes, Then exactly one versioned transition event with accepted reason codes is emitted, and unchanged accepted states emit none
Given the sampler test file, When inspected and run, Then every delay uses fake timers and the suite completes without any real sleep
Implement lifecycle-aware agent-health classification as a pure function

expected_outputs: agent-health.test.ts passes every classification state and boundary case

narrative.Action: Check first whether a canonical agent-health module already exists under src/lib/agents/ (PRD WI-4 says 'new or extend after checking ownership'). Implement the PRD Product-decision-4 classification order as a pure function over (persisted agent state, canonical runtime state, live tmux session set, review-status lifecycle, now): 1) resolver-corrupt/unreadable => unavailable with structured reason; 2) context saturated => wedged; 3) running/starting without tmux past the existing five-minute startup grace => dead; 4) work agent with kickoffDelivered === false past grace => stalled; 5) runtime waiting-on-human => waiting regardless of inactivity; 6) runtime idle/suspended including terminal-verdict advancing sessions => idle (plus lifecycle 'warm' when the canonical review-status classifier says warm); 7) runtime active => warning after 15 min without effective activity, stalled after 30; 8) otherwise healthy while live, idle when persisted but intentionally inactive. Expose real lastActivityAt; preserve consecutiveFailures, killCount, and contextPercent including 0 (no 0=>null coercion). Retire the inactivity-only 'stuck' logic in health-filtering.ts in favor of this function. Beware the known circular-ESM neighborhood around health-filtering.ts — keep the new module cycle-free (continue.json H5).

items.title: Given an idle, suspended, waiting-on-human, or warm terminal-verdict session inactive for over 30 minutes, When classified, Then the result is idle/waiting (never stalled or stuck) — intentional inactivity is not failure
Given a running-status agent with no tmux session past the five-minute startup grace, When classified, Then the result is dead; within grace, starting agents classify as healthy/starting
Given an active-runtime agent with no effective activity, When classified at 15 and 30 minutes, Then it returns warning then stalled at those boundaries
Given a corrupt/unreadable persisted state via the resolver, When classified, Then the result is unavailable with a structured reason code, not an omitted or healthy entry

Given an agent with contextPercent 0 and a real lastActivityAt, When its health snapshot is produced, Then contextPercent remains 0 (not null) and lastActivityAt reflects the actual activity timestamp, with consecutiveFailures and killCount preserved
